samples.reverse_paraphrase: The driver selects the first-order completeness chapter and imports its introduction, outline, complete-set, Henkin, Lindenbaum, model, identity, completeness, compactness and Löwenheim–Skolem sections in order.
samples.assessment: The chapter identity, complete classical first-order profile and completeness-section import order are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Completeness first says that every semantic consequence of a premise set is derivable from that set; soundness supplies the converse direction.
samples.assessment: Both formulations of completeness and their directions, the proof-theoretic meaning of consistency, compactness consequence and countable-model consequence retain their scope after OLCO-001 and OLCO-002.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The model-existence form says every syntactically consistent set of sentences is satisfiable, since consistency excludes derivability of a contradiction.
samples.assessment: Both formulations of completeness and their directions, the proof-theoretic meaning of consistency, compactness consequence and countable-model consequence retain their scope after OLCO-001 and OLCO-002.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Because derivations are finite, completeness implies that any semantic consequence already follows from a finite subset, which is the compactness consequence.
samples.assessment: Both formulations of completeness and their directions, the proof-theoretic meaning of consistency, compactness consequence and countable-model consequence retain their scope after OLCO-001 and OLCO-002.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The same construction directly proves compactness from finite satisfiability and yields a finite or denumerable model; OLCO-001 and OLCO-002 repair only the duplicated article and adjectival suffix.
samples.assessment: Both formulations of completeness and their directions, the proof-theoretic meaning of consistency, compactness consequence and countable-model consequence retain their scope after OLCO-001 and OLCO-002.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The outline switches from consequence-to-provability completeness to the equivalent task of showing every consistent sentence set has a model.
samples.assessment: The proof outline preserves atomic-model construction, negation, completion, Henkin witnesses, term models and identity quotienting after OLCO-003 through OLCO-005.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For atomic premises, interpret exactly the listed predicate tuples or propositional variables as true, producing a model of the set.
samples.assessment: The proof outline preserves atomic-model construction, negation, completion, Henkin witnesses, term models and identity quotienting after OLCO-003 through OLCO-005.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If not-B belongs to a consistent set, B cannot also belong, so the atomic construction that follows positive membership makes B false and not-B true.
samples.assessment: The proof outline preserves atomic-model construction, negation, completion, Henkin witnesses, term models and identity quotienting after OLCO-003 through OLCO-005.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Extend Gamma consistently until every sentence or its negation is present; this complete extension supports induction over compound formulas. OLCO-003 removes the erroneous atomic restriction and OLCO-004 restores the plural scope.
samples.assessment: The proof outline preserves atomic-model construction, negation, completion, Henkin witnesses, term models and identity quotienting after OLCO-003 through OLCO-005.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Existential witnesses may be unavailable in the original language, especially when it has too few or no constants.
samples.assessment: The proof outline preserves atomic-model construction, negation, completion, Henkin witnesses, term models and identity quotienting after OLCO-003 through OLCO-005.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The Henkin remedy adds countably many constants together with sentences tying them to quantified formulas while preserving consistency.
samples.assessment: The proof outline preserves atomic-model construction, negation, completion, Henkin witnesses, term models and identity quotienting after OLCO-003 through OLCO-005.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Taking all terms as the domain makes constants denote themselves and function symbols act by term formation.
samples.assessment: The proof outline preserves atomic-model construction, negation, completion, Henkin witnesses, term models and identity quotienting after OLCO-003 through OLCO-005.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Identity requires quotienting terms into classes determined by the completed theory Gamma-star, because syntactically different terms may be required equal; OLCO-005 restores Gamma-star.
samples.assessment: The proof outline preserves atomic-model construction, negation, completion, Henkin witnesses, term models and identity quotienting after OLCO-003 through OLCO-005.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A sentence set is complete exactly when, for every sentence A, it contains A or its negation.
samples.assessment: Complete consistent sets retain every membership equivalence, negation polarity, proof direction and dependency on derivability closure.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A complete consistent set contains exactly one of each sentence and its negation, and any consistent Gamma can be extended to such a Gamma-star.
samples.assessment: Complete consistent sets retain every membership equivalence, negation polarity, proof direction and dependency on derivability closure.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For complete consistent Gamma, derivability entails membership, negation membership complements membership, and conjunction, disjunction and implication have their expected membership conditions.
samples.assessment: Complete consistent sets retain every membership equivalence, negation polarity, proof direction and dependency on derivability closure.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If Gamma proves A but omits A, completeness places not-A in Gamma; explicit inclusion then derives not-A, contradicting consistency.
samples.assessment: Complete consistent sets retain every membership equivalence, negation polarity, proof direction and dependency on derivability closure.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Membership of a conjunction gives derivability of each conjunct, and derivability-to-membership returns both conjuncts to Gamma.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If a disjunction is in Gamma while neither disjunct is, completeness supplies both negations and the derivability facts make Gamma inconsistent.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If A-implies-B belongs to Gamma while A belongs and B does not, modus ponens plus completeness-derived not-B contradicts consistency.
